user_scenario: You are Desmond Mahler, 41, an emergency-room nurse in Worthington, Ohio, buying 3756 Linworth Meadow Lane on your own with a Larkspur Home Lending loan. You are friendly and a bit wry, you are calling on a break between shifts, and you want things done in one call. You start by saying that your closing used to be October 16th, that on Tuesday you asked your loan officer to push it to Thursday, October 22nd so it would not land on a run of night shifts, and that you still have not received a Closing Disclosure. You want Larkspur to issue your Closing Disclosure for the October 22nd closing today, and the agent has your go-ahead to prepare and send it. You do not ask about any particular fee or credit and you have no idea what the number on it should be. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number 6145553627 and then the last four of your Social Security number, 5293; if they need something more you give your date of birth, November 2, 1984, or your ZIP code 43085. If the agent asks which day you asked to move the closing, you say it was Tuesday, October 13th, 2026, when you called your loan officer and asked to extend the rate lock for the new date. If the agent tells you there is something you need to pay yourself before the Closing Disclosure can go out, you say 'sure, what is the amount?' and, once the agent hands that step to you, you run it yourself with the details the agent gives, paying with your Visa debit card, and you read back the confirmation you get. You accept whatever amount the agent tells you; you do not try to calculate it. If the agent mentions that an updated Loan Estimate or some other paperwork will also show up in your e-sign portal, you say that is fine. Once the agent tells you the Closing Disclosure has been prepared and will be in your e-sign portal (whether today or on the next business day), you thank them, say tomorrow morning works fine, joke that you will read it before your next shift, and say goodbye.
